recent_commits.message: The OpenScales OSD export now exists end-to-end. Work spanned three files:
recent_commits.body:
R/data_check_helpers.R — two shared, package-level helpers (so both the module and the converter can call them):

.osd_safe_code() — spec-valid code sanitizer.
.osd_code_and_provenance() — the three-tier provenance/code minting (dictionary → bare official code or curated METACHECK-; manuscript → METACHECK-; self-generated → METACHECK-GEN-), each with a human-readable provenance sentence.
inst/modules/codebook_check.R — rewrote .scales_to_osd(scale_groups, columns_df, labels_df, dict):

Spec-conformant structure: osd_version, definition.{scale_info, likert_options, items}, translations.en, plus a namespaced definition.metacheck block for provenance/confidence/source (kept out of the spec objects).
likert_options lets the codebook lead — decodes value_labels for range + anchor labels (source:"codebook"); falls back to observed min/max/n_unique from data_check stats (source:"observed"); omitted entirely when nothing is scale-shaped (no invention).
translations.en carries codebook item wording; text_key points at it per spec.
Named groups flagged write=TRUE; unnamed detections write=FALSE (report-only, no file).
R/psychds-convert.R — the file writer + cross-reference:

.osd_write_scales() writes one scales/{CODE}/{CODE}.osd per named scale (pretty JSON) under the dataset root.
.osd_write_readme_section() appends a "Psychometric scales" section to the root README.md explaining the three provenance markers and listing every scale (your "general README" decision).
Added metacheck:scale code + source to variableMeasured, so Psych-DS variables cross-reference their OSD definition.
n_scales added to the return list and completion message.

recent_commits.body:
Probed the follower/identity direction the survey pointed to (require the wide
row's column starts to be corroborated by the rows below). The classes do
separate -- furniture scores a clean 0.00, the real header 0.20 -- but 0.20 is
far too weak to found a threshold on, and per-column corroboration explains why:

    x=36.0 -> 15/15    x=284.7 -> 4/15    x=369.3 -> 3/15
    x=442.8 -> 1/15    x=549.8 -> 0/15  <- the P-value column

The rightmost column has ZERO corroboration anywhere in the table. Rel. risk and
P value are populated on exactly ONE row (the aggregate); the other 11 are
indented sub-rows that legitimately leave them blank. No vote-, follower-, or
corroboration-based rule can recover a column that occurs once -- the repetition
those algorithms need is not in the document.

So a geometry-only repair is impossible for this class, which retires the whole
family of attempts rather than inviting a fifth. What remains viable is evidence
from outside the geometry: header-TEXT typing (the header cells are recognisable
statistic labels, so they declare the column count directly), gated to
caption-anchored regions so it cannot fire on the ~1,700 prose pages the earlier
survey surfaced; or feeding header-derived x-positions to Camelot as explicit
columns. Both still need the 101-PDF guard-diff and canary sweep.

Records the cheap early check that would have saved two prototypes: count how
many rows populate the missing column; if it is 1, no geometric rule applies.

recent_commits.message: docs(findings): header-seeding PROTOTYPED then REJECTED by the corpus survey
recent_commits.body:
The proposed repair for plos_med T3's lost statistics columns -- seed boundaries
from the widest row, since the header declares every column -- was prototyped and
recovers the 5-column grid exactly. The vote tally shows the defect in one line:
the four TRUE boundaries carry 5, 13, 2 and 2 votes against a threshold of 7, so
exactly one clears it and the rule deletes all four.

The corpus survey then killed the fix. Scanning all 152 PDFs for the shape returns
1,707 pages, dominated by ordinary PROSE (modal=1 widest=4 wide_rows=1/22).
Inspecting one directly shows the "widest row" is a PAGE FOOTER --
"JAMANetworkOpen.2023;6(5): | (Reprinted) | May31,2023 | 10/12" -- above a
REFERENCES list. Seeding from it would fabricate a 4-column table out of a
bibliography on ~1,700 pages; the tail ("lost 29 columns") is the same artifact.

So the failing signal is not sparsity but IDENTITY: which row is actually a
header. A viable fix must establish that first (inside a caption-anchored region,
followed by data rows sharing its column starts -- _row_is_header is the natural
home) and be re-measured against this same 1,707-page population.

Second geometric shortcut rejected for this defect class, fourth across the
row-cluster family. Each looked excellent on its motivating paper; measurement,
not review, killed them. Recorded as a project lesson: print the winning row's
TEXT, not just its column count -- a footer, a running header and a wrapped
caption all look like "wide rows" to geometry.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): refuse a sign flip against a CI that cannot hold a negative (v2.4.123)
recent_commits.body:
docpluck rendered an IMPOSSIBLE F-statistic. maier Table 9's row is

    Target article | 1, 114 | 2.00 | .16 | N/A | .02 | [.00, .09]

-- an F, its p, its partial eta-squared, and the CI OF THE ETA-SQUARED. W0d
(recover_minus_via_ci_pairing) repairs a font corruption where a minus is read
as '2', accepting the flip when the corrected value lands inside a paired CI and
the literal does not. It paired the F-statistic with the eta-squared's CI: -.00
is inside [.00, .09] and 2.00 is not, so it fired, and the render carried

    F = -.00

An F-statistic is a ratio of sums of squares -- non-negative by construction --
so the output was not merely wrong but arithmetically impossible. Both text
channels confirm the source reads 2.00; the library manufactured the sign.

Fix: refuse the pairing when the CI's LOWER bound is >= 0. A wholly non-negative
interval cannot contain a negative, so containment is satisfiable only
degenerately (-.00 clipping the zero edge), which is evidence of MIS-PAIRING
rather than corruption. Keying on the interval's arithmetic instead of on F
specifically covers every non-negative statistic that can sit beside a
non-negative CI (F, chi-square, R2, eta2, odds ratios, variance components)
without enumerating them, and cannot disarm a genuine recovery -- a truly
negative estimate always has a CI admitting negatives.

Evidence:
- tests written against the unfixed code and watched FAIL, then pass;
- all 31 pre-existing W0d tests stay green, incl. the efendic B-column
  recoveries the rule exists for;
- corpus guard-diff, all 152 PDFs rendered twice (guard on vs off):
  2 false positives removed (the maier article and its ESCIcheck duplicate),
  0 regressions, every other paper byte-identical;
- suite 1962 passed, 3 xfail (the P1 table defects stay armed).

Companion to the REJECTED W0b-col recovery: that failed because column consensus
is not per-record evidence. This is the converse -- per-record containment IS the
right evidence, but only when the record paired is the right one. A containment
test silently assumes the CI belongs to the token it pairs with; verify that is

  WORD path: valid_rows=13 threshold=7 -> stable boundaries: [] -> 1 column

W0i's x-as-3 glyph recovery was rewriting RANGE BOUNDS as an operator inside
Camelot table cells. chan_feldman's Table-2 note rendered

    "Avoidance behaviour scores ranged from x to 15"

for a source that reads "from 3 to 15" -- the library DELETED a published scale
bound and wrote an operator in its place. Both text channels confirm the source
says 3; the raw-text channel rendered the same sentence correctly a hundred
lines earlier, so one document carried the same fact right and wrong at once.

trailing "to" could be a wrapped predictor ("Attitude 3 to risk"), and a lone
leading "from" is likewise ambiguous. A frame generalises across publishers.

_new_commits.message: fix(normalize): refuse a sign flip against a CI that cannot hold a negative (v2.4.123)
_new_commits.body:
docpluck rendered an IMPOSSIBLE F-statistic. maier Table 9's row is

    Target article | 1, 114 | 2.00 | .16 | N/A | .02 | [.00, .09]

-- an F, its p, its partial eta-squared, and the CI OF THE ETA-SQUARED. W0d
(recover_minus_via_ci_pairing) repairs a font corruption where a minus is read
as '2', accepting the flip when the corrected value lands inside a paired CI and
the literal does not. It paired the F-statistic with the eta-squared's CI: -.00
is inside [.00, .09] and 2.00 is not, so it fired, and the render carried

    F = -.00

An F-statistic is a ratio of sums of squares -- non-negative by construction --
so the output was not merely wrong but arithmetically impossible. Both text
channels confirm the source reads 2.00; the library manufactured the sign.

Fix: refuse the pairing when the CI's LOWER bound is >= 0. A wholly non-negative
interval cannot contain a negative, so containment is satisfiable only
degenerately (-.00 clipping the zero edge), which is evidence of MIS-PAIRING
rather than corruption. Keying on the interval's arithmetic instead of on F
specifically covers every non-negative statistic that can sit beside a
non-negative CI (F, chi-square, R2, eta2, odds ratios, variance components)
without enumerating them, and cannot disarm a genuine recovery -- a truly
negative estimate always has a CI admitting negatives.

Evidence:
- tests written against the unfixed code and watched FAIL, then pass;
- all 31 pre-existing W0d tests stay green, incl. the efendic B-column
  recoveries the rule exists for;
- corpus guard-diff, all 152 PDFs rendered twice (guard on vs off):
  2 false positives removed (the maier article and its ESCIcheck duplicate),
  0 regressions, every other paper byte-identical;
- suite 1962 passed, 3 xfail (the P1 table defects stay armed).

Companion to the REJECTED W0b-col recovery: that failed because column consensus
is not per-record evidence. This is the converse -- per-record containment IS the
right evidence, but only when the record paired is the right one. A containment
test silently assumes the CI belongs to the token it pairs with; verify that is
arithmetically possible first.

_new_commits.message: docs(findings): measure WHY plos_med T3 loses its columns — hierarchical sub-rows
_new_commits.body:
Probing _find_stable_column_boundaries on the real Table-3 band replaces the
earlier speculation (which guessed at midpoint scatter and the region path) with
a measurement, and it kills the proposed fix:

  WORD path: valid_rows=13 threshold=7 -> stable boundaries: [] -> 1 column
  BUCKETED(3/5/8pt): still 2 columns

The word path finds ZERO stable boundaries, so the region path is NOT the
culprit. The cause is the table's shape: Table 3 is hierarchical -- the header
and one aggregate row carry all 5 columns, while 11 of 13 rows are indented
sub-rows carrying only 3 (desaturation | 3/5 | 1/4). The Rel. risk and P value

they can never reach the vote threshold. Bucketing cannot help -- the votes do
not exist to be bucketed.

Lowering the fraction is explicitly NOT the fix (rule 20): 0.6 guards against
spurious boundaries from ragged prose rows, and a threshold admitting a 15%
column admits noise corpus-wide. The correct signature is that a column declared
by the HEADER is real even when most rows leave it empty -- seed boundaries from
the header rather than letting a majority vote delete them. That is an algorithm
change to a shared detector, so it gets its own gated cycle.

Also removes the now-superseded speculative section so the doc does not
contradict its own measurement, and records the class as a project lesson: a
stability-fraction vote assumes every column is populated in most rows, which
hierarchical/sub-row tables (common in clinical papers) violate by construction --
and the failure is silent, looking like a complete table with fewer columns.

    "Avoidance behaviour scores ranged from x to 15"

for a source that reads "from 3 to 15" -- the library DELETED a published scale
bound and wrote an operator in its place. Both text channels confirm the source
says 3; the raw-text channel rendered the same sentence correctly a hundred
lines earlier, so one document carried the same fact right and wrong at once.

Not paper-specific: any "from 3 to N" / "between 3 and N" reaching a table cell
was affected, in any publisher's paper.

Root cause: W0i's only pre-digit guard was _TIMES_REFERENCE_WORD_RE, a list of
reference NOUNS (Model|Study|Table|Figure|...) that makes "Model 3 predictor" a
genuine ordinal. "from" is not a reference noun, so the guard had nothing to
say, while "from 3 to" matches W0i's letter-space-3-space-letter signature
exactly. A vocabulary list cannot defend a grammatical position -- it is always
missing the next word.

Fix: guard on the grammatical FRAME instead. A range is from|between BEFORE the
digit AND to|and|through|until AFTER it, with BOTH halves required -- a lone
trailing "to" could be a wrapped predictor ("Attitude 3 to risk"), and a lone
leading "from" is likewise ambiguous. A frame generalises across publishers.

Evidence:
- new tests written against the unfixed code and watched FAIL, then pass;
- full-corpus pdftotext sweep (all 152 PDFs): 8 range-frame-with-3 sites across
  5 distinct articles, out of 380 range frames overall -- all 5 pinned as
  regression cases. The sweep is why the guard covers "between ... and": maier's
  Bayes factors and bmc_med_3's lesion diameters use it, and a from-only guard
  would have left them exposed;
- targeted production-path guard-diff (each paper rendered twice, guard on vs
  off, so every difference is attributable to this change): 1 false positive
  removed, 0 regressions, all 8 canaries byte-identical;
- suite: 1959 passed, 3 xfail (the two P1 pinned table defects stay armed).

highlights.message: docs(findings): the plos_med column loss has a STRUCTURAL ceiling, not a threshold one
highlights.body:
Probed the follower/identity direction the survey pointed to (require the wide
row's column starts to be corroborated by the rows below). The classes do
separate -- furniture scores a clean 0.00, the real header 0.20 -- but 0.20 is
far too weak to found a threshold on, and per-column corroboration explains why:

    x=36.0 -> 15/15    x=284.7 -> 4/15    x=369.3 -> 3/15
    x=442.8 -> 1/15    x=549.8 -> 0/15  <- the P-value column

The rightmost column has ZERO corroboration anywhere in the table. Rel. risk and
P value are populated on exactly ONE row (the aggregate); the other 11 are
indented sub-rows that legitimately leave them blank. No vote-, follower-, or
corroboration-based rule can recover a column that occurs once -- the repetition
those algorithms need is not in the document.

So a geometry-only repair is impossible for this class, which retires the whole
family of attempts rather than inviting a fifth. What remains viable is evidence
from outside the geometry: header-TEXT typing (the header cells are recognisable
statistic labels, so they declare the column count directly), gated to
caption-anchored regions so it cannot fire on the ~1,700 prose pages the earlier
survey surfaced; or feeding header-derived x-positions to Camelot as explicit
columns. Both still need the 101-PDF guard-diff and canary sweep.

Records the cheap early check that would have saved two prototypes: count how
many rows populate the missing column; if it is 1, no geometric rule applies.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
highlights.author: Gilad Feldman

highlights.message: docs(findings): header-seeding PROTOTYPED then REJECTED by the corpus survey
highlights.body:
The proposed repair for plos_med T3's lost statistics columns -- seed boundaries
from the widest row, since the header declares every column -- was prototyped and
recovers the 5-column grid exactly. The vote tally shows the defect in one line:
the four TRUE boundaries carry 5, 13, 2 and 2 votes against a threshold of 7, so
exactly one clears it and the rule deletes all four.

The corpus survey then killed the fix. Scanning all 152 PDFs for the shape returns
1,707 pages, dominated by ordinary PROSE (modal=1 widest=4 wide_rows=1/22).
Inspecting one directly shows the "widest row" is a PAGE FOOTER --
"JAMANetworkOpen.2023;6(5): | (Reprinted) | May31,2023 | 10/12" -- above a
REFERENCES list. Seeding from it would fabricate a 4-column table out of a
bibliography on ~1,700 pages; the tail ("lost 29 columns") is the same artifact.

So the failing signal is not sparsity but IDENTITY: which row is actually a
header. A viable fix must establish that first (inside a caption-anchored region,
followed by data rows sharing its column starts -- _row_is_header is the natural
home) and be re-measured against this same 1,707-page population.

Second geometric shortcut rejected for this defect class, fourth across the
row-cluster family. Each looked excellent on its motivating paper; measurement,
not review, killed them. Recorded as a project lesson: print the winning row's
TEXT, not just its column count -- a footer, a running header and a wrapped
caption all look like "wide rows" to geometry.

highlights.message: fix(normalize): refuse a sign flip against a CI that cannot hold a negative (v2.4.123)
highlights.body:
docpluck rendered an IMPOSSIBLE F-statistic. maier Table 9's row is

    Target article | 1, 114 | 2.00 | .16 | N/A | .02 | [.00, .09]

-- an F, its p, its partial eta-squared, and the CI OF THE ETA-SQUARED. W0d
(recover_minus_via_ci_pairing) repairs a font corruption where a minus is read
as '2', accepting the flip when the corrected value lands inside a paired CI and
the literal does not. It paired the F-statistic with the eta-squared's CI: -.00
is inside [.00, .09] and 2.00 is not, so it fired, and the render carried

    F = -.00

An F-statistic is a ratio of sums of squares -- non-negative by construction --
so the output was not merely wrong but arithmetically impossible. Both text
channels confirm the source reads 2.00; the library manufactured the sign.

Fix: refuse the pairing when the CI's LOWER bound is >= 0. A wholly non-negative
interval cannot contain a negative, so containment is satisfiable only
degenerately (-.00 clipping the zero edge), which is evidence of MIS-PAIRING
rather than corruption. Keying on the interval's arithmetic instead of on F
specifically covers every non-negative statistic that can sit beside a
non-negative CI (F, chi-square, R2, eta2, odds ratios, variance components)
without enumerating them, and cannot disarm a genuine recovery -- a truly
negative estimate always has a CI admitting negatives.

Evidence:
- tests written against the unfixed code and watched FAIL, then pass;
- all 31 pre-existing W0d tests stay green, incl. the efendic B-column
  recoveries the rule exists for;
- corpus guard-diff, all 152 PDFs rendered twice (guard on vs off):
  2 false positives removed (the maier article and its ESCIcheck duplicate),
  0 regressions, every other paper byte-identical;
- suite 1962 passed, 3 xfail (the P1 table defects stay armed).

Companion to the REJECTED W0b-col recovery: that failed because column consensus
is not per-record evidence. This is the converse -- per-record containment IS the
right evidence, but only when the record paired is the right one. A containment
test silently assumes the CI belongs to the token it pairs with; verify that is
arithmetically possible first.

Found by the run-5 canary audit against the AI multimodal gold.

highlights.message: docs(findings): measure WHY plos_med T3 loses its columns — hierarchical sub-rows
highlights.body:
Probing _find_stable_column_boundaries on the real Table-3 band replaces the
earlier speculation (which guessed at midpoint scatter and the region path) with
a measurement, and it kills the proposed fix:

  WORD path: valid_rows=13 threshold=7 -> stable boundaries: [] -> 1 column
  BUCKETED(3/5/8pt): still 2 columns

The word path finds ZERO stable boundaries, so the region path is NOT the
culprit. The cause is the table's shape: Table 3 is hierarchical -- the header
and one aggregate row carry all 5 columns, while 11 of 13 rows are indented
sub-rows carrying only 3 (desaturation | 3/5 | 1/4). The Rel. risk and P value
columns appear in 2/13 rows = 15%, far below COLUMN_STABILITY_FRACTION = 0.6, so
they can never reach the vote threshold. Bucketing cannot help -- the votes do
not exist to be bucketed.

Lowering the fraction is explicitly NOT the fix (rule 20): 0.6 guards against
spurious boundaries from ragged prose rows, and a threshold admitting a 15%
column admits noise corpus-wide. The correct signature is that a column declared
by the HEADER is real even when most rows leave it empty -- seed boundaries from
the header rather than letting a majority vote delete them. That is an algorithm
change to a shared detector, so it gets its own gated cycle.

Also removes the now-superseded speculative section so the doc does not
contradict its own measurement, and records the class as a project lesson: a
stability-fraction vote assumes every column is populated in most rows, which
hierarchical/sub-row tables (common in clinical papers) violate by construction --
and the failure is silent, looking like a complete table with fewer columns.

highlights.message: docs(findings): plos_med T3/T5 silently drop their statistics columns (capture layer)
highlights.body:
Confirms a run-5 cycle-1 audit finding (this one is REAL, unlike the alpha and
heading-level claims from the same sweep). Table 3 renders 3 of 5 columns: the
Rel. risk (95% CI) and P value columns -- the paper's primary results -- are
absent from the .md with no truncation marker. Table 5 loses its entire GA
column. A reader sees a complete-looking table with the effect sizes gone.

Diagnosed to the CAPTURE layer: the values never reach extract_pdf_structured
(no cell and no raw_text contains 1.19 or 4.31), so no render-side fix can
recover them.

The data IS present and clean in BOTH text channels -- the layout channel has
five cleanly separated x-positions (36.0/282.8/367.5/449.7/559.7) for that row --
so this is recoverable, not OCR-tier. What fails is Camelot stream detection:
plain auto-detect returns a 7x2 grid with all four data columns crushed into one
cell. Notably Table 2 of the SAME paper resolves 9 columns via the auto-detect
path; the two tables that collapse are the two that went through the
region-driven path.

Filed rather than fixed: the natural repair (prefer the whitespace/char grid when
Camelot returns a degenerate one) is explicitly the not-yet-wired change flagged
in TABLE_EXTRACTION_VERSION v2.4.3, and it is a selection-class change -- the
family with this project's worst regression history (v2.4.6 global matching fixed
bmc_med_3 but regressed chan_feldman T6 and reshuffled ~24 papers). Two probe
attempts to instrument _find_stable_column_boundaries on the real region timed out
(>5 min layout extraction); the doc records the exact next step and the gate.

highlights.message: docs(findings): one typographic heading level rendered at two markdown levels
highlights.body:
The run-5 cycle-1 audit filed 4 SECTION-BOUNDARY findings claiming chan_feldman's
'Interpersonal forgiveness' et al. should be ## not ###. Checking the source PDF's
typography DISPROVES that claim: those headings are MyriadPro-BoldIt 10.0pt while
Method/Results/Discussion are MyriadPro-Bold 10.5pt -- a different font and size, so
### is defensible and the gold's flat ## is the less faithful rendering. Acting on
the audit would have meant promoting correct output to match a flattened gold.

Disproving it surfaced a REAL defect the audit missed: docpluck splits ONE
typographic level across TWO markdown levels with no typographic basis. Background,
Original hypotheses, and Evaluation criteria render as ## while Interpersonal
forgiveness, Pre-registration, Power analysis and Participants render as ### -- all
of them BoldIt 10.0pt at x0=48.0. Background and Interpersonal forgiveness are
typographically indistinguishable and land on different levels, so the rendered
hierarchy is not a faithful model of the document.

Filed rather than fixed: the inconsistency is unambiguous, but which tier maps to
## is a product decision (mapping tier-2 uniformly to ### is typographically
faithful but demotes Background, which golds and readers expect at ##). Heading
promotion is also a shared code path with a history of corpus-wide regressions, so
any fix needs a heading-only guard-diff plus the 8-canary sweep.

Also re-scopes the broad-read "furniture leak" class to B6 in TRIAGE: 11 of 13
instances are mid-sentence column splices, not own-line strippable furniture, and
imada's 'irrespective of the Introduction' exists in NEITHER text channel.

highlights.message: fix(normalize): a range bound is a number, not an interaction operator (v2.4.122)
highlights.body:
W0i's x-as-3 glyph recovery was rewriting RANGE BOUNDS as an operator inside
Camelot table cells. chan_feldman's Table-2 note rendered

    "Avoidance behaviour scores ranged from x to 15"

for a source that reads "from 3 to 15" -- the library DELETED a published scale
bound and wrote an operator in its place. Both text channels confirm the source
says 3; the raw-text channel rendered the same sentence correctly a hundred
lines earlier, so one document carried the same fact right and wrong at once.

Not paper-specific: any "from 3 to N" / "between 3 and N" reaching a table cell
was affected, in any publisher's paper.

Root cause: W0i's only pre-digit guard was _TIMES_REFERENCE_WORD_RE, a list of
reference NOUNS (Model|Study|Table|Figure|...) that makes "Model 3 predictor" a
genuine ordinal. "from" is not a reference noun, so the guard had nothing to
say, while "from 3 to" matches W0i's letter-space-3-space-letter signature
exactly. A vocabulary list cannot defend a grammatical position -- it is always
missing the next word.

Fix: guard on the grammatical FRAME instead. A range is from|between BEFORE the
digit AND to|and|through|until AFTER it, with BOTH halves required -- a lone
trailing "to" could be a wrapped predictor ("Attitude 3 to risk"), and a lone
leading "from" is likewise ambiguous. A frame generalises across publishers.

Evidence:
- new tests written against the unfixed code and watched FAIL, then pass;
- full-corpus pdftotext sweep (all 152 PDFs): 8 range-frame-with-3 sites across
  5 distinct articles, out of 380 range frames overall -- all 5 pinned as
  regression cases. The sweep is why the guard covers "between ... and": maier's

highlights.body:
Continues the corpus-driven falsification of the row-cluster chain-merge fix.

REJECTED (all measured corpus-wide or on verified cases):
  - row span:            legit rows reach 94pt+ (xiao T4 r2)

  - distinct_y count:    continuous 2->50, classes interleave (legit 26 > chain 23)

exact row whose mis-splitting broke 9 tests, so this variant would repeat the

sub-lines never share columns but the pattern is strictly PERIODIC.

separates the rest — but ip_feldman T10 r1 (chain) reaches 0.251 against chan T6
r2 (legit) at 0.270. A 0.019 margin on six hand-picked rows will not survive the
corpus; it needs the same survey that killed distinct_y, over rows whose class is
VERIFIED rather than assumed, and must be rejected if the margin does not widen.

viable directions are content typing and split-then-re-merge on column occupancy.

is destroyed at clustering time, before any guard sees it. So this gates a
meaningful slice of the table backlog, not one paper.

DISTINCT_Y THRESHOLD REJECTED. distinct_y looked like a clean discriminator on

and hand-inspecting the decision band shows the classes genuinely interleave —

rows, while ip_feldman T10 r1 (dy=27) is a real chain merge fusing '.29*** -.21***
.07' with Discussion prose. A legitimate row at 26 sits above a chain merge at 23.

Also recorded as a caution against labelling by assumption: two rows I first
called legitimate were not (sci_rep_2 T1 r13 is absorbed body prose; chen T9 r1
is the sparse label 'Study 2:'). Verifying them flipped the conclusion twice.

Conclusion: row height, gap size and y-level count are ALL insufficient. The
discriminator must use content or column occupancy, not geometry alone.

highlights.message: fix(tables,normalize): grid-guard false negatives + a 50x ReDoS (v2.4.121)
highlights.body:
TABLE_EXTRACTION_VERSION -> 2.4.10. NORMALIZATION_VERSION deliberately
unchanged: the normalize fix is complexity-only, matching is byte-identical.

Two false-negative classes in the guard that decides whether a whitespace/char
grid is a real DATA table:

(a) _CAPTION_LABEL_RE was UNANCHORED, so a mid-sentence CROSS-REFERENCE in a
    footnote/prose cell ("...al. (2007) in Table 8.", "...in Figure 2. We
    summarized...") read as an absorbed caption and condemned the whole grid.
    An absorbed caption always BEGINS its cell; a reference has sentence text
    before it. Anchored to ^\s*, matching the discipline
    camelot_extract._CAPTION_ROW_PATTERN already documents (its comment notes
    anchoring is why an inline "see Table 2" does not match).

(b) the clean-data-cell test matched a SINGLE numeric token, so every
    multi-token APA COMPOSITE scored as non-data: 2.84 [1.89] (mean [SD]),
    3.47 [1.23] (170) (mean [SD] (n)), 2.84 +/- 1.89, 0.42***. A descriptives
    table built from them scored clean_data_rows=0 and was discarded as prose.
    Replaced the shape regex with a NUMERIC-DOMINANCE test (_cell_is_clean_data:
    digit-bearing AND free of substantive words), which generalises instead of
    chasing each composite with another alternation. The prose side is unmoved,
    so absorbed body text is still rejected.

101-PDF guard-diff: 24 tables recover (up from 20 at v2.4.120), 0 regressed,
0 foreign-caption acceptances.

A SECOND quadratic regex, and why the first fix looked complete but wasn't:
v2.4.120 bounded _CI_UPPER_DROPPED_RE and reported the ReDoS resolved. It was
not — normalize_text still scaled ~4-5x per doubling. It was missed because the
check was an absolute WALL-CLOCK budget, which passed alone and failed only
under parallel load, so it read as flakiness. Rewritten as a SCALING RATIO
(load-independent: contention inflates both measurements together) it failed
consistently, turning noise into signal.

Instrumenting every COMPILED pattern's .sub() via re.compile interception (a
module-level sweep misses these — they live inside a list literal, and reported
0.000s) attributed 3.165s of 3.7s at n=20000 to the Royal Society running-footer
pattern in _WATERMARK_PATTERNS, whose leading unbounded \d+ starts a match
attempt at every digit and then fails. Bounding it to \d{1,6} (a page number is
never longer) is ~1370x faster on the pattern (4.53s -> 0.0033s) and ~50x
end-to-end (normalize_text 4.85s -> 0.044s at n=20000), now genuinely linear at
~2.0x per doubling, with both real footer forms matched identically. A
lookahead-anchored variant was tried first and MEASURED WORSE (6.4s vs 3.2s) —
discarded rather than reasoned about.

This permanently removes the flakiness from
test_regex_no_catastrophic_backtracking, which prior handoffs recorded as a
load-sensitive perf test. It was a real, long-standing performance defect all
along. Full suite also runs ~10 min faster (24:51 vs 37:19).

highlights.message: test(tables): pin the _cluster_into_rows chain-merge defect (attempted fix REVERTED)
highlights.body:
_cluster_into_rows measures the y-gap to the PREVIOUS WORD, not the row's anchor.
Words sort by (top, x0), so in a table with wrapped or vertically staggered cells
the running 'previous top' creeps forward in sub-threshold steps and the threshold
is never crossed — an unbounded chain merge. chan_feldman Table 3 holds 266 words
at 47 distinct y-positions with 0.3-7.4pt gaps against an 11.4pt threshold, and
clusters into 3 rows spanning 240pt: a 10-row table smeared into 3, which then
fails the grid guards on its own 'merits' and falls to the truncating raw_text
fallback.

The anchor-relative fix was implemented and REVERTED. In isolation it looked
excellent (chan T3 3->22 rows; T2 0->108 cells; T9 0->14 cells; maier T8/T11
gained cells) but it broke 9 real-PDF tests across 4 files, because a real row
can legitimately be TALL: xiao Table 4's row 2 spans 94.4pt as a multi-line
stacked data block, and a hard anchor cap shatters it. The previous-word test
under-splits; a naive anchor cap over-splits. Neither rule alone is correct.

Ships the reproduction as xfail(strict) so the defect stays visible and a correct
fix XPASSes loudly, plus three plain-assert companions pinning behaviour that must
not regress while it is solved. FINDINGS doc records the measurements and three
candidate directions (re-merge on shared column occupancy; explicit chain-merge
signature detection; derive the row grid from the most stable column).

highlights.message: fix(tables): a table's own caption no longer condemns its own table (v2.4.120)
highlights.body:
RC-T cycle 4. _whitespace_grid_is_clean rejects any grid containing a
"Table N."/"Figure N." cell — the signature of a region that absorbed a
NEIGHBOURING table's caption. But _region_for_caption builds every region as
_union(caption_bbox, geom_bbox), so a caption-anchored region ALWAYS contains
its own caption by construction. The guard therefore condemned EVERY region
grid: whitespace_cells returned 0 cells corpus-wide (19/19 chan_feldman+maier
regions) and each table fell to the raw_text fallback, which truncates rows.
The guard's own comment said the marker proves the region absorbed "an adjacent
table's (or its own) caption" — the "or its own" clause was the bug.

The exemption is IDENTITY-based, not position-based: the anchoring caption's
number is threaded from the region spec / region.caption_match into the guard,
and a caption cell is exempt only when it names THAT exact number, sits in a
leading row, and is the first such match — per-CELL, and opt-in so the
auto-detect path keeps the strict legacy behaviour.

A position-only draft was written and REJECTED in cross-model review (codex);
all three of its holes reproduced locally: a neighbour's caption in a leading
row blessed as "own" (publishing another table's data), (r,c) sort order picking
the leftmost caption on side-by-side pages, and a whole-ROW exemption letting a
second Table/Figure caption ride along. Each is pinned by a regression test.

text-shape recovery: a dotless, leading-zero-free canonical threshold
(05/01/001) after `<`/`>`/`≤`/`≥` is never legitimate notation. Four guards
(never `=`; canonical set only; no longer-number continuation;
significance-clause context) keep the 10-fold-wrong-number FP impossible on
the shapes the corpus actually contains (only other dotless sites corpus-wide
are legitimate `P = 1` exact values, excluded by the operator guard). Wired
channels 1+3; NORMALIZATION_VERSION 1.9.45.
